notes.57: gemach (58), usually 'ease, comfort', seems to mean little more than 'thing, event' here. gelouben (82) is taken as 'grant'; it could be 'believe'.

nodes.text: how in Jerusalem there came to pass
a serpent grew up in it
which drank dry all the wells
that were there in the city;
Because of this the people came
he ordered the people to go and
When it had drunk it all up,
I know he bound it while it slept.
It was a great [work of] God's power
that the serpent spoke to him,
[which] you will build in one year,
Now tell it to me at once,
or I will have you destroyed.
A beast goes about on Lebanon;
I will tell you exactly how you [should do it]:
make a cord out of them;
it will be sharp and keen;
very evenly it must [split] in two,
